latin: Sicut de solo intellectu uere dicitur quod est ignis, et quod est aqua, quod est motus, et quod est status, ita de sola anima uere dicitur quod frigefit, quod calefit, quod stat, quod mouetur.
translation: Just as it is truly said of the intellect alone that it is fire, and that it is water, that it is motion, and that it is rest, so it is truly said of the soul alone that it is cooled, that it is heated, that it stands still, that it is moved.
translation_note: The Latin pairs static predicates for intellect (ignis, aqua, motus, status) with corresponding verbs of undergoing for soul (frigefit, calefit, stat, mouetur); the rendering keeps that pairing.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch13, from Latin at farmer1998:20762
doctrine: The thesis draws a parallel between intellect and soul through opposed grammatical modes: the intellect alone is truly said to be fire, water, motion, and rest (predicated as what it is), while the soul alone is truly said to be cooled, heated, to stand still, and to be moved (predicated as what happens to it) (farmer1998:20762). Farmer records no explanatory note on this thesis and no cross-reference to another (per the sources consulted).
historiography: The one located mention is a footnote in the German study Erkenntnistheorie und christliche Kabbalah, which cites 3>35 immediately after 3>23 in a list of consecutive theses, without separate discussion (kabbalah_paradigma:1771).
not_established: Farmer offers no note on this thesis, and no scholarly discussion of its content beyond the bare citation was located: not established by the sources consulted (farmer1998:20762; kabbalah_paradigma:1771).
